subject.title: Support session-level environment variables for ACP sessions

question: Should OpenClaw expose a per-spawn `sessions_spawn.env` API for ACP sessions, or keep env injection limited to configured/trusted surfaces such as per-agent env?
rationale: The requested API is useful but can pass credentials into host subprocess environments, so automation should not choose the trust model, allowed sources, redaction rules, or interaction with credential scrubbing.

options.title: Design a safe per-spawn env contract
options.body: Approve `sessions_spawn.env` only with validation, redaction, blocked keys or SecretRef-style handling, session freshness semantics, and tests across tool, ACP manager, and ACPX paths.

options.title: Route to per-agent env only
options.body: Keep this issue open or close it as superseded only if maintainers decide the configured `agents.list[].env` path is the supported solution for these use cases.

options.title: Reject per-spawn env
options.body: Close the request if maintainers decide model-callable ACP env injection is too broad for OpenClaw’s security boundary.

recommendation.title: Design a safe per-spawn env contract
recommendation.body: Approve `sessions_spawn.env` only with validation, redaction, blocked keys or SecretRef-style handling, session freshness semantics, and tests across tool, ACP manager, and ACPX paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ACPX runtime ownership plus adjacent credential-boundary context makes this the best available routing candidate from the inspected history.
